blocks.name: bit-membership
blocks.note: Numeric-uint32 and signed-bit-pattern forms are both explicit; bit-pattern forms avoid unnecessary unsigned scalar coercion.

blocks.name: fixed-width-word-composition
blocks.note: Generic, caller-range-proven, and initialization-prepared cross-word shift profiles coexist. Configured/fixed shift distances can precompute 32-count or count-32 once, deleting one SUB from every hot shift.

blocks.name: first-next-set-bit
blocks.note: Set-bit/cardinality profiles reuse caller-owned lane facts. A known high lane uses firstSetHighBitIndex32 without lane selection; cardinalityClass32 applies whenever exactly one lane remains relevant, including two-lane callers that already proved the other lane empty.

blocks.name: popcount
blocks.note: Exact popcount profiles now cover fixed fused SWAR, set-bit sparsity, high-lane emptiness, high<=10 table lookup, and their combined distribution/cache profile. Selection remains explicit from configured width, occupancy distribution, and cache evidence.

blocks.name: coordinate-decode
blocks.note: Coordinate decode has table-backed generic profiles and initialization-selected power-of-two geometry profiles. Power-of-two columns use mask/shift and can omit coordinate tables when no other consumer needs them.

blocks.name: legal-landing-cell
blocks.note: Landing/legality profiles now cover maintained landing arrays and packed-support-derived geometry. When packed 3-bit support is already independently required and a column field shift is prepared/owned, heightFromPacked3Support32 can eliminate a duplicate heights[] mirror; landingCellFromPacked3Support32 derives the physical cell in 6 cycles. Maintained landingCell32 remains preferred when its total load plus update traffic is cheaper.

blocks.name: winning-line-test
blocks.note: Winning-line containment supports signed/unsigned one- and two-lane forms. Initialization should partition immutable required masks into low-only, high-only, and cross-lane groups; single-lane groups use maskContainsI32/maskContains32 directly, leaving two-lane functions only for masks that actually span lanes.

blocks.name: apply-undo-state-transition
blocks.note: Apply/undo profiles cover caller-owned ply, known cells, packed/caller-carried support/playable state, and caller-owned residual-frame restoration. When parent residual classes are already live from independent node work and parent status is proved before descent, restoreCallerOwnedResidualFrame32 permits class/status history streams to be omitted; spill/frame traffic must be qualified at the recursive governing unit.

blocks.name: hash-mix32
blocks.note: Hashing profiles include direct two-/three-coordinate indices, fused triple-key publication, and separable ordered tuple fingerprints. publish3x32Locator32 applies when a canonical-key producer must publish three exact coordinates to caller-owned scratch anyway: the locator consumes those live scalars and avoids immediately reloading the scratch. Exact equality remains identity. Generic/exact separable tuple builders and parent-delta updates cover residual-class tuples.

blocks.name: transposition-cache-probe
blocks.note: TT/cache probing retains prepared indices and exact identity. Proven hit updates may store only the value. Exact triple open addressing can fold occupancy into an impossible key0 sentinel. Two-word dense-key interners can preserve producer-owned key scalars through direct indexing, exact probing, and publication: probe2x32IdSlot32 performs no source-key reloads, and publish2x32IdSlot32 writes a new dense pair/hash slot directly from those scalars.

blocks.name: canonical-reflection-symmetry
blocks.note: Reflection may be recomputed by configured register/table profiles or maintained incrementally by recursion. canonicalPrimaryCompare32 enables primary-first orbit routing: a cheap exact coordinate can select orientation before expensive secondary reflection/comparison, with secondary tie-break work only when required. A caller-owned reflected-support scalar may advance by one ADD and needs no undo.

blocks.name: frontier-antichain-normalization
blocks.note: Frontier normalization now has signed/unsigned, one-/two-lane, and seeded lazy-compaction profiles. Signed bit-pattern storage is cheapest when selectable; Uint32 owners retain bit-31 correctness while still avoiding the first candidate and accepted-prefix rewrites.

blocks.name: residual-transition
blocks.note: Residual transitions support both class-major and action-major prepared-base layouts. Class-major fits fixed-class/varying-action loops; action-major fits the pinned fixed-action/varying-class residual loop. Initialization transpose cost remains explicit.

blocks.name: move-order-selection
blocks.note: Move-order/selection profiles include prepared move-slot indexing, exact/scalar candidate counts, and run-grouped immutable-word reuse. reuseGroupedWord32 exploits incidence layouts already ordered by word index: one load serves the entire consecutive run, with no cache object or mutable mirror.

blocks.name: alpha-beta-bound-update
blocks.note: Alpha-beta profiles now exploit the full child-update window invariant. Test raw score for cutoff first; if it continues, test score against the active bound. A bound-raising/lowering child is automatically the new best, deleting a separate best comparison; only the residual fail-low/fail-high region needs best-only comparison.

blocks.name: shared-atomic-claim-release
blocks.note: Atomic claim has direct-CAS and load-first high-mismatch profiles. Load-first filters observed mismatches before locked RMW work but remains conservative: stale mismatches may return false and stale matches are revalidated by CAS. Release retains notify/no-notify ownership profiles.

blocks.name: shared-queue-enqueue-dequeue
blocks.note: Queue sequence comparisons are performed in the Int32 domain. Equality-first nonblocking profiles retain their fast-path reduction, while dequeue-ready values are explicitly normalized across 0x7fffffff -> -2147483648 rollover. Owned/shared and blocking/nonblocking profiles otherwise remain unchanged.

blocks.name: capacity-growth-rehash
blocks.note: Capacity growth keeps allocation and rehash costs explicit. rehashOverwrite32 now performs only migration; new capacity is caller-known from newMask and is not reconstructed/returned by the primitive.
